summary: The test code is syntactically correct and should compile and run without errors. It uses Playwright APIs correctly with proper awaiting of asynchronous assertions. The testCaseIds are preserved in the test titles. However, selectors rely on placeholder text 'Category Name' which needs real category names to work in practice. Assumptions about the existence and class names of elements like '.product-item' and generic 'heading' role usage introduce selector fragility. Assertions check for basic navigation and element presence but do not validate that filtered products exactly match the selected category. This reduces assertion strength. No test data injection or reuse mechanisms are implemented, affecting maintainability and reusability. The code shows straightforward, readable test structure but could improve test data handling and selector robustness.

issues.description: Selectors are based on placeholder text 'Category Name' which is not replaced with actual category names. This makes the selectors invalid for actual test runs.
issues.recommendation: Replace 'Category Name' with actual category names or parametrize the tests to accept dynamic category inputs.

issues.description: Assertions verify URL and heading text but do not confirm that the displayed products strictly belong to the selected category.
issues.recommendation: Add assertions that check product attributes or categories to ensure only relevant products are shown.

issues.description: Using generic role 'heading' to verify category heading text can be fragile if multiple headings exist on the page.
issues.recommendation: Use more specific selectors for the category heading, e.g., by combining role with accessible names or using a test-specific locator.

issues.description: Test data such as category names is hardcoded as placeholder strings, reducing reusability and scalability.
issues.recommendation: Implement reusable test fixtures or parameterize tests to handle different category names dynamically.

recommendations: Parameterize category names to avoid hardcoded placeholders in selectors and assertions.
Enhance assertions to verify filtered products match the selected category, improving test reliability.
Use more specific selectors for headings to avoid ambiguity and improve test robustness.
Incorporate test data management strategies to improve maintainability and reusability.
